fact: Preparatory workshops for Gabon's future national AI strategy closed in Libreville on 30 September 2026 with 22 challenges and 36 recommendations from six UNDP-supported groups; the ministry and UNDP will next draft the strategy, action plan, financing and indicators, and the outputs are a diagnostic, not a finished strategy.

The digital-economy ministry and UNDP announced on 26 September 2026 consultations in Libreville from 28 to 30 September to prepare a national AI strategy, feeding its formulation, review and finalisation; no budget or adoption date is given.
The digital-economy ministry's secretary-general opened workshops on drawing up Gabon's national AI strategy in Libreville on 28 September 2026, with UNDP as partner.

The digital-economy minister closed three days of work on drawing up Gabon's future national AI strategy on 30 September 2026; UNDP said the document presented is a preliminary diagnostic, not a finished strategy, to be consolidated and validated in later steps.

The ministry and UNDP held a three-day co-creation workshop as the first step of Gabon's future national AI strategy, with the draft strategy, a validation workshop and government adoption still to come.

The UNESCO National Commission with the national technical committee for AI (CTN-IA) opened a two-day workshop on 20 March 2025 to support the drawing up of a national AI strategy for Gabon, with strategic recommendations expected at its close (AGP).
